get_term.description: Look a term up by its id, IRI or OLS link: its label, definition, synonyms, cross-references to other vocabularies (MeSH, ICD-10, UMLS...), older ids, whether it is obsolete and what replaced it, and every annotation. An id OLS doesn't know comes back with 'found' false.

mock_response.definition: A programmed cell death process which begins when a cell receives an internal (e.g. DNA damage) or external signal (e.g. an extracellular death ligand), and proceeds through a series of biochemical events (signaling pathway phase) which trigger an execution phase. The execution phase is the last step of an apoptotic process, and is typically characterized by rounding-up of the cell, retraction of pseudopodes, reduction of cellular volume (pyknosis), chromatin condensation, nuclear fragmentation (karyorrhexis), plasma membrane blebbing and fragmentation of the cell into apoptotic bodies. When the execution phase is completed, the cell has died.
descriptions: A programmed cell death process which begins when a cell receives an internal (e.g. DNA damage) or external signal (e.g. an extracellular death ligand), and proceeds through a series of biochemical events (signaling pathway phase) which trigger an execution phase. The execution phase is the last step of an apoptotic process, and is typically characterized by rounding-up of the cell, retraction of pseudopodes, reduction of cellular volume (pyknosis), chromatin condensation, nuclear fragmentation (karyorrhexis), plasma membrane blebbing and fragmentation of the cell into apoptotic bodies. When the execution phase is completed, the cell has died.
mock_response.label: apoptotic process

terms.definition: A molecular process that can be carried out by the action of a single macromolecular machine, usually via direct physical interactions with other molecular entities. Function in this sense denotes an action, or activity, that a gene product (or a complex) performs.
terms.label: molecular_function

terms.definition: A location, relative to cellular compartments and structures, occupied by a macromolecular machine. There are three types of cellular components described in the gene ontology: (1) the cellular anatomical entity where a gene product carries out a molecular function (e.g., plasma membrane, cytoskeleton) or membrane-enclosed compartments (e.g., mitochondrion); (2) virion components, where viral proteins act, and (3) the stable macromolecular complexes of which gene product are parts (e.g., the clathrin complex).
terms.label: cellular_component

terms.definition: A biological process is the execution of a genetically-encoded biological module or program. It consists of all the steps required to achieve the specific biological objective of the module. A biological process is accomplished by a particular set of molecular functions carried out by specific gene products (or macromolecular complexes), often in a highly regulated manner and in a particular temporal sequence.
terms.label: biological_process

parameters.description: Terms (classes) are what most annotation uses. Properties are the relations between terms.

parameters.description: Only match the whole text, not words within it. With 'Search in' set to label and synonyms, only terms named exactly this.

parameters.description: Which parts of a term to search. Leave empty for all of them.
parameters.name: fields

parameters.description: Leave out obsolete terms, or find only them (to check what replaced a retired term).
parameters.name: obsolete

parameters.description: Skip copies of a term that other ontologies import, so each term is listed once, from the ontology that defines it.
parameters.name: defined_here_only

parameters.description: Only find terms under this one, such as MONDO:0005015 (diabetes mellitus) for kinds of diabetes: its id or IRI.
parameters.name: under_term

parameters.description: With 'Under term': follow subclass (is a) links only, or part of and the other hierarchical links too.
parameters.name: relations

options.label: Subclass and part of links (is a, part of, develops from)

parameters.description: The most rows to return, up to 1,000. The result says how many there are in all.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Which page of results to return, from 1.
parameters.name: page

has_more.description: True when there are more on later pages.

summary.description: One line saying what was found.

description.description: The first description OLS holds for it: usually its definition, sometimes a comment.

id.description: The term's id, such as GO:0006915: its OBO id where it has one. Every Term field takes it.

iri.description: The term's IRI, such as http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_0006915: its permanent, unique name.

is_defining_ontology.description: True for the ontology that defines it; false for a copy another imports.

label.description: The term's name, such as apoptotic process.

ontology_id.description: The id of the ontology it is in, such as go.

ontology_prefix.description: The ontology's prefix, such as GO.

type.description: What it is: class (a term), objectProperty or dataProperty (a relation), or individual.

total.description: How many matches there are in all.

description: Search and browse about 290 biomedical ontologies in EMBL-EBI's Ontology Lookup Service (OLS): the Gene Ontology, ChEBI, EFO, the Human Phenotype Ontology, MONDO, Uberon, NCIT and more. Find terms by name or synonym, map free text to its best term, look a term up by its id (definition, synonyms, cross-references, obsolete or replaced), walk its parents, children, ancestors, descendants and paths to the root, list its other relationships, and see each ontology's version, size and licence. No account or API key required.
